content.text:
The gap is large: the web app is ~30k lines across 17 pages and 80+ components (streaming chat, interactive quiz/goal/question cards, artifact viewers, sandbox/code execution, speech, learner profile, benchmarks, sharing, marketing pages). Mobile is ~2.4k lines: non-streaming chat, sessions list, saved artifacts, settings.

Full parity isn't a single task — and much of the web app (sandbox runtime, mermaid/webgpu, marketing/blog pages, OAuth callback routing) either can't or shouldn't be ported to React Native as-is. Let me get your scope before I build.

questions.question: Which web features should the RN app replicate?

options.label: Core chat parity
options.description: Streaming responses, stop/retry, model selector, persona-composed system prompt, auto-titling, session recovery — bringing mobile chat up to Chat.tsx behavior minus rich cards.

options.label: Interactive learning cards
options.description: Quiz / question / goal / flashcard renderers with the tag-parsing + result-feedback loop, ported to RN views.

options.label: Settings + learner profile
options.description: Full settings surface: providers/models tab, teacher persona editor, UI settings, learner profile & insights.

options.label: Artifacts & sharing
options.description: Artifact viewer/browser, export/import, shared-session links, markdown+code rendering.

questions.question: How should shared logic be handled?

options.label: Extract to shared/ (Recommended)
options.description: Move platform-agnostic keating/* logic (persona, tool-call-normalizer, srs, goals, starter-prompts…) into shared/ so web and mobile import one copy. More upfront work, no drift.

options.label: Copy into mobile/src
options.description: Duplicate the logic into mobile. Faster now, diverges over time — how keating-core.ts is already handled.

options.description: I pick the biggest win from your scope and implement it end-to-end with tests, then we iterate.

The native UI is purpose-built with React Native. It does not embed the web app. The adapter in `src/lib/keating-core.ts` reuses the web app's dependency-free pedagogy engine directly, so offline study plans, concept maps, quizzes, topic fallbacks, and domain-specific lesson phases stay aligned across both clients.

`src/lib/persona.ts` mirrors the web app's persona/protocol split: the editable teacher persona (John Keating by default) supplies the voice, and the fixed protocol in `src/lib/system-prompt.ts` supplies the pedagogy, so rewriting the persona in Settings can never remove the teaching loop.

## Streaming responses

Replies stream token by token. The web app streams through `@earendil-works/pi-ai`, which does not run under Metro, so `src/lib/provider-client.ts` implements SSE directly for the OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, and Gemini wire formats and reads the response body with `expo/fetch` (React Native's built-in `fetch` exposes no readable stream). Deltas are buffered and committed to React state on a fixed cadence so the chat list is not re-rendered per token. Servers that ignore `stream: true` and answer with one JSON body still work through a whole-payload fallback. Stopping a response keeps whatever text already arrived.

Built the highest-value slice: **streaming chat + the editable teacher persona**.

**What changed**

- `src/lib/provider-client.ts` — SSE streaming for all three wire formats (OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Gemini `:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse`). - `src/lib/persona.ts` + `persona-storage.ts` — the web's John Keating persona, copied. Split so the pure part stays RN-import-free (`bun test` can't import AsyncStorage).
- `src/lib/system-prompt.ts` — now the persona/protocol split from web: editable voice + fixed pedagogy, composed per request.
- `KeatingProvider.tsx` — appends a placeholder assistant message, streams into it via `expo/fetch`, and flushes buffered deltas on a 60ms cadence rather than per token. Stopping keeps partial text; a failure removes the half-message.
- Chat screen + `MessageBubble` — pulsing caret while streaming, actions hidden until done, non-animated follow-scroll during streams.
- Settings — persona editor with save / "Restore John Keating".

- React Native's built-in `fetch` exposes no readable body, which is why streaming goes through `expo/fetch`. Anything else that streams must use it too.
- `bun`'s `Response` always has a body, so the "no stream body" branch can't be covered by these tests — it's covered indirectly by the content-based fallback test.

## Interactive cards

Replies can carry `<keating-quiz />`, `<keating-question />`, and `<keating-goal />` tags in the same double-encoded JSON wire format the web tools emit. The web app produces them from browser tools; the mobile app has no tool loop, so the teaching protocol in `src/lib/system-prompt.ts` asks the model to emit them inline and `src/lib/interactive-tags.ts` parses them back out. Malformed payloads are dropped rather than shown as raw markup, and a tag still mid-stream stays hidden until its closing `/>` arrives.

Quizzes are graded locally by `src/lib/quiz-grading.ts` — exactly for multiple choice, true/false, and multi-blank fill-ins, and by a partial-credit heuristic for written answers, which the teacher then judges properly when the results are reported back as a learner turn. Submitting a card sends that report as a normal message, so the whole exchange stays in the transcript. Answers are also held in memory by `src/state/card-state.ts` so a completed card scrolled off screen comes back completed.

The web app's scene, image, animation, and flashcard deck cards are not ported yet.

- `mobile/src/lib/interactive-tags.ts` — parses `<keating-quiz|question|goal json="…" />` in the same double-encoded wire format the web tools emit, plus tolerant normalizers (infers question type from options, folds a missing MC key back into the choices, defaults goal step kind/status/order). Malformed or empty payloads are dropped, never rendered as raw markup.
- `mobile/src/lib/quiz-grading.ts` — the web renderer's `questionCredit` / `isOpenEnded` / `isCorrect` ported verbatim (Levenshtein + keyword + bigram recall for open-ended), plus `scoreQuiz` and the two report builders that become the learner's reply turn.

**UI**: `components/cards/QuizCard.tsx`, `QuestionCard.tsx`, `GoalCard.tsx`, and `MessageContent.tsx`, which splits an assistant turn into markdown runs and cards. `MessageBubble` now renders through it and takes an `onCardResult` that the chat screen wires straight to `sendMessage` — so submitting a quiz posts the graded summary as a normal user message and the teacher answers it. Open-ended answers are explicitly flagged in that report for the teacher to grade by meaning.

**Feedback loop details**: cards stay inert while the reply is still streaming, and a half-arrived tag is trimmed from the markdown so JSON never flashes on screen. `state/card-state.ts` holds submitted answers in memory keyed by message id + segment index, so a completed card that scrolls out of the FlatList comes back completed; `clearLearningData` wipes it.

**Protocol**: since mobile has no tool loop, `system-prompt.ts` gained `INTERACTIVE_CARD_PROTOCOL` with a worked example per tag. A test feeds the documented quiz example back through the parser, so the prompt and the parser can't drift apart.

Verified: `bun test` 43 pass / 0 fail (17 new), `tsc --noEmit` clean, `bun run export:android` produces a 4.2MB Hermes bundle. Not run on a device — the on-screen feel of the cards is unconfirmed.
